etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Either borrowed from Middle French abscondre or directly from Latin abscondō (“hide”); formed from abs, ab (“away”) + condō (“put together, store”), from con- (“together”) + *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place, set”).
senses: (intransitive) To flee, often secretly; to steal away. [From mid 16th century.]
(intransitive) To hide, to be in hiding or concealment.
